title: Strict quotient augmentation of ordinary integral pullback on all complexes
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$ and a uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] set $C_{W,n}=(R/t^n)_W$ for $n\geq1$, $B_W=\varprojlim_n C_{W,n}$, with quotient projections $\pi_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $c_f:f^{-1}B_Y\to B_X$ be the adjoint of the limit map $B_Y\to f_*B_X$ whose $n$-th projection is the constant-section map after $\pi_{Y,n}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Use module sheaves, sheaf tensor and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $f_B^*M=B_X\otimes_{f^{-1}B_Y}f^{-1}M$, with its ordinary module adjunction [def-sf-ordinary-integral-pullback-construction].

For every cochain complex $Q$ of $B_Y$-modules, put $Q_n=Q\otimes_{B_Y}C_{Y,n}$ and $T_f(Q)_n=\operatorname{Res}_{\pi_{X,n}}f_n^*Q_n$, where $f_n^*$ is the finite-coefficient module pullback and the strict transitions $T_f(Q)_{n+1}\to T_f(Q)_n$ are induced by the actual coefficient reductions [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. There is a unique natural transformation of strict complex towers
$$a:\Delta f_B^*\longrightarrow T_f$$
on the category of all $B_Y$-cochain complexes, normalized on local tensor generators by
$$a_{Q,n}(b\otimes q)=1\otimes(q\otimes\pi_{X,n}(b)).$$
Here $q$ is an inverse-image local section, and the right side uses the inverse-image comparison for sheaf tensor; equivalently the adjunction-unit image of any section $q$ maps to the finite-pullback unit image of $q\otimes1$. Every $a_{Q,n}$ is $B_X$-linear and commutes with differentials. Writing $r_{Q,n}$ for the displayed transition and $v:Q\to Q'$ for any chain map, its strict identities are
$$r_{Q,n}a_{Q,n+1}=a_{Q,n},\qquad T_f(v)_n a_{Q,n}=a_{Q',n}f_B^*(v).$$
Consequently $a_Q=\prod_n a_{Q,n}$ satisfies $(1-s)a_Q=0$ and determines the natural chain map
$$\alpha_Q:f_B^*Q\longrightarrow\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:T_f(Q)_{\rm prod}\to T_f(Q)_{\rm prod})[-1]$$
whose unshifted product coordinate is $a_Q$ and whose shifted product coordinate is zero, with the cone conventions of [def-weil-derived-limit]. No flatness, boundedness, constructibility or completeness of $Q$ is required.

proof.text: Identify the completed coefficient map with IntegralAmbient.coefficientMap by the unique finite-projection equations. Uniqueness of left adjoints gives an isomorphism from the specified ordinary module pullback to IntegralAmbient.pull; its unit equation identifies original adjunction-unit sections with pullSection. Apply this comparison termwise, then IntegralOnSlice.augmentation, then IntegralAmbient.pullTowerIso. These are natural transformations of actual strict towers, so their composite is natural and retains all quotient transitions. The two normalization formulas for augmentation and pullTowerModel send a unit generator to the stated finite-pullback generator of x tensor 1; scalar insertion of 1 acts trivially.

proof.text: For uniqueness, compare any normalized transformation with this composite at each complex, level and degree. Apply the injective module-adjunction Hom equivalence; equality of its sections on every original site object is exactly the given normalization formula. Extensionality successively for module maps, chain maps, tower maps and natural transformations proves equality. No generation assertion on sections of an arbitrary target-site object is needed.

It adds no new nodes and has no cycle (the item is not in the 707-node closure of its dependencies). I read every cited statement and checked all nine steps. Step 1: the coefficient square pi_X c_f = c_n F(pi_Y) holds because both sides have the same adjunct by the limit equation for rho; the reduction square holds because both maps extend the same constant-presheaf map. Step 2: u(xq) = pi_X(c_f x) u(q). The inverse-image tensor comparison (clause 1) is used only to read the statement's notation for the generator formula. Step 3: the pairing is A-bilinear and the tensor universal property gives a B-linear map. Steps 4 and 5: chain-map property, naturality and strict transitions r a_{n+1} = a_n, all checked on pure tensors. Step 6: uniqueness from injectivity of the tensor bijection, and also from the Hom bijection of the module adjunction; this avoids the objectwise local-generation claim made in the Lean docstring. Step 7: products exist sectionwise and (1-s)a = 0. Step 8: I checked the cone signs against def-weil-abstract-derived-category (C(f)^r = L^r + K^{r+1}, shift differential -d): Cone(w)[-1] has d(z,x) = (-dz - wx, dx), and alpha = (0, a) is a chain map. Step 9: the mapping-cocone map is natural. Edge cases checked: Q = 0, f = id, n = 1, t-torsion and non-flat M, M = B_Y, unbounded complexes, empty schemes. Lean source checked: OrdinaryCompletedIntegralPullback.lean:276-298 is the same assertion with proof sorry, so there is nothing to attach. lean.statement:
theorem ordinaryIntegralQuotientAugmentation_existsUnique :
    ∃! a : ordinaryIntegralPullComplex l E f ⋙
        (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ : CochainComplex (integralTowerModules l E X) ℤ ⥤ _) ⟶
      integralOperationsPullbackTowerFunctor l E f,
      ∀ (P : CochainComplex (integralTowerModules l E Y) ℤ) (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ)
        (V : Y.ProEt) (x : (P.X i).val.obj (op V)),
        (((a.app P).app (op n)).f i).val.app (op ((proEtaleBaseChange f).obj V))
          (((ordinaryIntegralModuleAdjunction l E f).unit.app (P.X i)).val.app (op V) x) =
        integralOperationsPullbackGenerator l E f n
          (((unrestrictedIntegralFiniteComplex l E Y n).obj P).X i) V
          (unrestrictedIntegralTensorSection l E Y n (P.X i) (op V) 1 x)
lean.note: Existing statement in the module of def-sf-ordinary-integral-pullback-construction, lines 276-298, with the strict product and zero-coordinate mapping-cocone construction at lines 306-370.
